why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, looking for probes that appear in both. The builder brief reuses the verifier's probes. Builder step 2 tells it to test that "`node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`". Verifier Check 1 runs `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and passes only on `HELLO, ADA!` plus a newline. That is the same input and expected output. Builder step 1 also fixes the no-flag output as "`Hello, Ada!\n`", which is the PASS value in verifier Check 2. The builder brief also lists `Ada --shout` and the missing-name exit code 2, which match the verifier's advisory probes. The criterion does allow telling the builder to write its own tests and to run `npm test`. It does not allow giving the builder the checker's exact inputs and expected outputs, so the builder brief carries the checker's methods.
